name: ManimGX
cost: Free. Its own code is MIT; native wheels include x264 and are GPL-3.0-or-later as a whole
works_with: macOS, Linux, Windows and the browser. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor
short: A fast animation engine that turns Manim-style Python into 1080p60 math and 3D videos, built for agents to write.
what: ManimGX uses Manim Community Edition's API, so your agent writes familiar Python, and a Rust and wgpu engine renders the MP4. It handles 2D and 3D together, LaTeX or Typst without a LaTeX install, and speech synced to animation. `manimgx inspect` gives agents storyboards to check their work.
who: Teachers, explainer-video makers and anyone with existing Manim scenes who wants them rendered much faster. Skip it if you don't want to work in Python.

steps.title: Install it
steps.text: Fonts, typesetting and video encoding are included.

steps.title: Write a scene
steps.code:
import manimgx as m


class Hello3D(m.ThreeDScene):
    def construct(self) -> None:
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=65 * m.DEGREES, theta=-45 * m.DEGREES)
        self.begin_ambient_camera_rotation(rate=0.5)
        cube = m.Cube(side_length=3, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)
        self.play(m.Create(cube), run_time=2)
        self.wait(4)

try.label: From the README
try.text: Once it is installed, ask: "make a 3D animation of the solar system, and open it."

watch: The README also offers a prompt that tells your agent to follow a remote llms.txt file. The pip install above does not need it.
Native wheels are GPL-3.0-or-later as a whole because they include x264. Check that fits how you plan to ship.
